subject: Latency spike 2027-04-01 — routing/maintenance classification dispute
messages:
From: Connor Blake <ops@skylineware.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Increased tail latency & 5xxs during 04/01 maintenance window — request for SLA credit

Hi Alex,

We saw a sustained increase in tail latency and a cluster of 5xx responses for our production endpoints between 16:40 and 17:25 PDT on 2027-04-01. Our telemetry shows ~18% requests above SLA latency and a small spike in error rate that impacted checkout flows.

Skyline's account rep pointed us to Redwood's maintenance policy — you're marking the window as a planned route maintenance by a third-party backbone. We're disputing that classification: the routing shift appears to have been sudden and affected only your US-west endpoints (we saw retries, token churn, and partial failures). The impact here was material (we delayed a release).

Can you confirm how Redwood calculated uptime apportionment and whether Skyline is eligible for a full SLA credit rather than a partial apportionment? We need the calculation and any traceback you have.

Attaching our summary (small CSV excerpt) for your review.

Thanks,
Connor Blake
Head of Site Reliability, SkylineWare
ops@skylineware.com

Attachment: skyline-telemetry-20270401.csv (CSV)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 19:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Increased tail latency & 5xxs during 04/01 maintenance window — request for SLA credit

Connor — thanks for the note and for the csv. Sorry for the impact.

Quick note on next steps: I've looped in our SRE (Diego) and your CSM (Marissa) so we can pull the raw ingress traces and the routing decision logs. We're going to produce a short apportionment report that shows which portion of the latency/error delta we attributed to our runtime versus an upstream backbone routing event.

Can you confirm whether Skyline used the us-west-2 region exclusively during the window (or if you had multi-region fallback enabled)? That helps us with the apportionment math.

I'll follow up before EOD Pacific with an interim readout.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Connor Blake <ops@skylineware.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Increased tail latency & 5xxs during 04/01 maintenance window — routing analysis attached

Hi all — I pulled the relevant traces and routing logs. Summary:

- Observation window: 2027-04-01T23:40:00Z — 2027-04-01T00:25:00Z (PDT local: 16:40–17:25).
- We observed a sudden BGP route change at 16:42 PDT from Backbone provider "NorthSeaNet" affecting our edge POP in us-west-2; following the change, there were transient TCP retransmits and an elevated SYN/ACK latency for ~30s.
- After the initial route flap, an automated failover in our edge routing stack moved ~42% of active connections to a secondary path that has higher RTT. That failover is intentional to reduce total error rate but it increased tail latency for some sessions.
- We saw ~0.9% increase in 5xxs that correlate with mid-flight connection resets during the route flap.

Attachments: sre-routing-analysis-20270402.pdf (includes per-pop timelines and the traces CSV). Also attaching the raw ingress spans (ingress-traces-20270401.csv).

Apportionment rationale (short): the initial route flap was caused by a third-party backbone maintenance/instability; however, our edge failover decision and longer-lived session handling amplified the latency for a subset of requests. Per our SLA, third-party backbone outages are eligible for partial exclusion, but customer-visible impact caused by our failover behavior is within Redwood's control for apportionment. Based on our standard calculation, we estimate a 62% apportionment to third-party (credit excluded) and 38% to Redwood (eligible for credit). Using Skyline's recorded downtime window, that yields a partial credit of 38% of the impacted SLA bucket.

Diego Fernandez
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai

Attachment: sre-routing-analysis-20270402.pdf (PDF), ingress-traces-20270401.csv (CSV)

From: Connor Blake <ops@skylineware.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased tail latency & 5xxs during 04/01 maintenance window — routing analysis attached

Diego — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the attachments. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) Skyline did have multi-region fallback configured, but traffic remained pinned to us-west-2 because session affinity plus a persistent DNS TTL meant our clients didn't switch quickly. We still saw customer-impacting latency in the US for ~45 minutes.
2) We disagree with the apportionment math. The backbone route flap was not scheduled maintenance; it was an operational change that caused customer-visible errors. We expect Redwood to assign full credit when a third-party event causes degraded service that impacts our SLA.

We appreciate the analysis but we want Redwood to reclassify this as a "service incident" (not a third-party maintenance) and issue a full SLA credit. We've escalated this to our execs because we took a release pause.

Please advise on the timeline for a final ruling or a call with your ops leads.

— Connor
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Connor Blake <ops@skylineware.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Increased tail latency & 5xxs during 04/01 maintenance window — routing analysis attached

Connor — thanks for the candid feedback and apologies again for the disruption. I understand the business impact and the escalation to your execs. 

Two actions from Redwood today: 
- We will schedule an expedited post-incident audit call (SRE + Networking + Skyline ops) for Monday 2027-04-04 at 09:00 PDT. Monica (our CS lead) will send the invite and prep questions.
- As a one-time goodwill gesture while the audit completes, Redwood will issue a provisional credit equivalent to 50% of the impacted SLA bucket for April 1. This is independent of the formal apportionment calculation and is intended to reduce immediate friction. The provisional credit will be finalized (increased to full credit or adjusted downward) after the audit findings, but we will not reverse a goodwill credit upward.

If that sounds acceptable, we'll proceed with the call and the provisional credit posting in the partner billing queue today. I want to be explicit: our current engineering analysis attributes part of the impact to the third-party route flap and part to our edge failover behavior — that is why our default apportionment yields a partial credit. The audit will validate timelines and we will share raw logs.

Thank you for pushing on this — we take SLA disputes seriously and want to reconcile quickly.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
